analysis:
The change is documentation-only (docs/architecture/inference.md). The supplied base text covers lines 1-797. The head-side edits are at lines 404-410, mostly in the base ranges, and 1050-1070. The 1050-1070 range falls outside the supplied base text and the patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not fully examine it. No executable code, authorization logic, crypto or configuration is modified.

The edit at base 404-407 documents Super load-gate behavior. `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad` releases retained free KV segments and drops the MLX buffer cache once before the first eviction or a no-idle refusal, and pre-accept counts retained segments as reachable.

The new section at head 1050 describes parked free 64 MiB KV segments:
- They are kept per pool, up to min(2 GiB, grant/8), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge.
- New segments use zero-fill-on-demand host pages.

Security-relevant questions for later review, which are not findings because the code is not in evidence:
1. T-028 residual-data exposure: reinstalling parked segments across requests could expose prior-request KV, which holds consumer prompt data (A-001). I cannot confirm whether segments are zeroed or overwritten before reuse.
2. Cross-tenant reuse: parked segments are reinstalled by size class. It is unverified whether they are scoped by tenant, although the reuse is intra-process.
3. Memory accounting: parked bytes sit outside the ledger, up to 2 GiB per pool. This could weaken admission and OOM bounds (T-029-style availability), although the documentation claims they are reclaimed on the load path.

The retained-segment reclaim during load and eviction is a documentation claim only. The implementation in the provider-swift sources should be reviewed to check the zeroing/overwrite guarantee and the ledger exclusion. Because the head excerpt is truncated, deeper review of the code change is warranted.
